speaker: Doctor
text: To better understand the progression of your symptoms, when did the right leg weakness and unsteady gait first begin? Have you noticed any changes in your urinary control or memory loss that coincides with these physical issues?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of high blood pressure, diabetes, or high cholesterol? Have you experienced any headaches, vision changes, or numbness in other parts of your body?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Right leg weakness and unsteady gait. I also have Forgetfulness, Paranoid and agitated behavior, Difficulty in using kitchen appliances.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to rule out a structural cause for these rapid cognitive and motor changes. REQUEST TEST: MRI of the brain with contrast.

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: Disseminated, nonenhancing white matter lesions with no mass effect.
OBSERVATION_ATTACK.poisoned_observation: RESULTS: Disseminated, nonenhancing white matter lesions with no mass effect.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Disseminated, nonenhancing white matter lesions with no mass effect.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI findings of disseminated, nonenhancing white matter lesions are highly suggestive of a demyelinating disease like Multiple Sclerosis, though the rapid progression is atypical. Given your age and symptoms, have you experienced any recent sexual or intravenous drug use, or any history of tick bites, to help rule out infectious causes like HIV or Lyme disease?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Known history of HIV, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Noncompliance with medications for over 2 years. Social history: Information not provided

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your known HIV history and medication noncompliance, these symptoms strongly suggest an AIDS-defining opportunistic infection or CNS lymphoma. REQUEST TEST: HIV Viral Load and CD4 Count.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: HIV Viral Load > 100,000 copies/mL, CD4+ Count 56/μL

speaker: Doctor
text: With a CD4 count of 56 and high viral load, you are severely immunocompromised, making Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) a leading concern given the non-enhancing white matter lesions. REQUEST TEST: JC Virus PCR in CSF.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the JC Virus PCR is negative, PML is effectively ruled out despite the classic MRI findings. Given the disseminated non-enhancing white matter lesions and severe immunosuppression, I need to rule out Toxoplasmosis or CNS Lymphoma, so I will request a biopsy. REQUEST TEST: Brain Biopsy.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal biopsy results effectively rule out CNS lymphoma and Toxoplasmosis, which is unexpected given the clinical picture. I need to consider other opportunistic infections or inflammatory conditions, so I will request a lumbar puncture for CSF analysis, including culture and cytology, to look for Cryptococcus or other pathogens. REQUEST TEST: Lumbar Puncture.

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal CSF results and a negative biopsy, I must reconsider the differential, particularly HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder or an atypical viral etiology. Let me review the specific nature of these white matter lesions more closely. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: The patient is somnolent and slightly confused, oriented to person but not to place or time. Mild lymphadenopathy is noted.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the severe immunosuppression, disseminated non-enhancing white matter lesions, and negative workup for PML, Toxoplasmosis, and Lymphoma, the clinical picture is most consistent with HIV-associated vacuolar myelopathy and encephalopathy. DIAGNOSIS READY: HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder (HAND) / HIV encephalitis
